method: component sessions write the playbook, dataset sessions the notes (s08, D32 B)

sessions.notes:
- List every column/table whose name resembles a question term and check hints/description for the one that actually means it; near-synonym columns often measure something different — pick by meaning, not name similarity.
- If a table looks like a precomputed "all"/union table, verify it covers every key needed (compare its distinct keys against the full per-entity tables/columns); convenience tables can silently omit entities.
- Don't hand-write a mapping from outside knowledge; if a reference table encodes the same fact, join to it and confirm coverage instead of trusting a manual list.
sessions.rationale: Addresses: pancancer_atlas/3 (wrong near-synonym column vs. the one hints point to); stockmarket/2&3 (convenience union table excludes some per-ticker tables, silently dropping entities); stockindex/3 (hardcoded lookup instead of validating against an available reference table). General verification habits, no dataset names/columns, no question text or SQL copied.

sessions.notes:
- When two tables' keys share a common part but differ by a fixed prefix/suffix, derive the exact transform (replace prefix A with prefix B, strip a known affix) and join on full-string equality — don't extract only the trailing/leading digits and compare those; two differently-prefixed key families can share a numeric suffix, causing spurious matches or duplicated rows that silently change counts/averages downstream.
- Sanity-check the join: compare distinct key counts on each side and the joined row count against the base table's count to catch mismatches before computing metrics.
sessions.rationale: Root cause was matching keys by regex-extracted numeric suffix instead of the exact prefix-replacement transform implied by the schema, which mismatched/duplicated rows and shifted the pooled average. Generalized to any prefixed/suffixed key pair, plus a verification habit, without naming the dataset.

sessions.notes:
- To pull a value from a templated sentence, anchor a regex to the fixed words around it (capture after a label, to next punctuation); a loose `LIKE '%word%'`/`split_part` on one phrase matches some templates and misses or misjoins the rest.
- Before matching free-text names/titles to a phrase, normalize both sides alike (lowercase, strip non-letters/spaces), not raw substring compare — sources vary spacing/casing/punctuation across duplicate rows.
- For "X itself" filters, extract the full field and test equality, not containment — containment also matches longer names that include X.
sessions.rationale: Covers patents/2 & patents/3 (anchored regex vs loose LIKE/split_part misreading fields) and music_brainz/2 (normalize before substring match). Trimmed under 600 chars.

sessions.notes:
- Identify which date/entity the window phrase refers to (e.g. "closed/signed in X" windows the end event's date, "opened/created in X" windows the start) — don't default to the easiest column.
- Build windows half-open: `>= start AND < next_start`; never `<= last_day`, which is midnight and drops same-day timestamps after 00:00.
- "Among/who did X (at least N times)" defines the population: require X to exist (inner join/having), don't LEFT JOIN+COALESCE missing rows in at a default.
- Row-level filters (nulls, keys) go in WHERE before grouping; thresholds on counts/sums go in HAVING after.
sessions.rationale: Addresses crmarenapro/8 (LEFT JOIN+COALESCE wrongly admitting non-qualifying entities vs required inner join), crmarenapro/9 & /12 (window applied to wrong date column), and yelp/6 (inclusive <= midnight bound dropping same-day late timestamps vs half-open <).

sessions.notes:
- Include columns needed to disambiguate rows and to show the ranking/filter metric, not only the named entity: if an entity can repeat (versions, records), add the attribute used to pick "latest"/"top one" and the value used to order or filter.
- Match the reference's row grain: one row per entity after grouping, not per raw join row; use a window + LIMIT 1 per key to pick one row, not DISTINCT.
- If a text value can contain a comma or quote, apply CSV-style escaping: wrap it in double quotes, doubling embedded quotes.
- Drop plumbing columns (join keys, flags) from the final SELECT.
sessions.rationale: Fixes: deps_dev_v1/2 and github_repos/4 dropped a disambiguating/metric column the reference kept — bullets 1-2. bookreview/2 needed CSV quoting for a comma-containing title — bullet 3. Bullet 4 trims extras.

sessions.notes:
- Output formatting (applies to ANY question whose answer is book titles, however phrased — "list the titles", "which books...", "return all matching books", etc., not only questions literally saying "list titles"): gold answers always CSV-encode the title column — if a title contains a comma, wrap the whole title in double quotes and double any internal double quotes (standard CSV field quoting). ~34/200 titles in bookreview_books_info contain a comma. Always apply this transform to any returned title column before submitting, even in pass_through mode; do not return the raw title text when the question's answer is a list of book titles.
- Join key: `books_info.book_id` is `bookid_N`, `review.purchase_id` is `purchaseid_N`. Join by extracting the trailing integer from each side (`substring(... from '[0-9]+$')::int`) and comparing as integers, not by concatenating a prefix or using LIKE/wildcard on ids.
- `categories` is a string-encoded list, e.g. `["Books", "Literature & Fiction", "Poetry"]`. Match a category by its exact quoted element (regex on `"CategoryName"`), not a loose `LIKE '%CategoryName%'`, since category names can be substrings of each other and of surrounding text.
- Book language lives only in the templated `details` text, with many phrasings ("written in English", "available in English", "is in English", "this English-language ...", bilingual "available in both English and X"). Use a word-bounded regex (`\mEnglish\M`) on the language name so all phrasings match while avoiding partial-word false matches; bilingual English editions still count as English.
- `review_time` is text in one consistent date-time format across all rows (1997-2023); cast directly with `::timestamp`.
- Compute average rating per book by grouping individual `bookreview_review` rows (joined via the extracted id) and taking `avg(rating)`; never use any pre-aggregated rating field on `books_info`.
sessions.rationale: The single failure (bookreview/2) was a "shape" mismatch: the agent returned raw titles instead of CSV-quoting the one title containing a comma. The prior note only mentioned CSV-encoding for questions literally phrased "list the titles", so the agent missed applying it to a differently-phrased question ("Which ... books ... Return all matching books"). I broadened that note to state the CSV-quoting rule applies to any question whose answer is a set of book titles, regardless of phrasing, and to apply it even under pass_through mode. Kept the other already-verified notes (join key extraction, categories quoted-element matching, language word-boundary regex, review_time format, average-rating computation from raw review rows) unchanged since they aren't implicated in this failure and are used correctly elsewhere (e.g. the passing bookreview/3 query already follows them).

sessions.notes:
- Transfer-count rankings (casehistory__c, field__c='Owner Assignment'): only 12 of 165 rows have oldvalue__c not null (a real transfer); the rest are first assignments (oldvalue__c null). When ranking agents by transfer count, the pool is agents who appear at least once as oldvalue__c in the window — never add zero-transfer agents at 0 via LEFT JOIN/COALESCE; "never transferred" is undefined for this metric, not a real 0, and floods the ranking with ties.
- "Handled/managed a case" = agent appears as newvalue__c (received it) in an Owner Assignment row; count distinct case ids per agent, not rows.
- Sales-cycle: Opportunity.CreatedDate -> Contract.CompanySignedDate via Opportunity.ContractID__c = Contract.Id (exact 1:1 key, every non-null ContractID__c matches one contract.Id once '#'/whitespace stripped). When a period is given for when deals "closed/were made", filter on CompanySignedDate falling in it, not CreatedDate.
- Case-closure-time windows ("past N quarters/months" for closure speed): filter on the case's createddate (when opened), not closeddate; closeddate (non-null) is only used to compute duration.
- OwnerId, ContractID__c etc. on opportunity/order/contract carry a leading '#' on ~1 in 5 rows — normalize with ltrim(trim(x),'#') before grouping/aggregating by the id too, not just before joins.
- Compute closure/handle duration as an exact interval in seconds (extract(epoch from closeddate::timestamptz - createddate::timestamptz)), not truncated whole days — most cases close within hours, so day-truncation ties nearly everything at 0.
- knowledge__kav "policy" articles (summary equals title, or starts "Policy") have faq_answer__c split into numbered paragraphs by blank lines; a rule naming a product2.Name applies only when that product is on the quote/order reviewed; rules naming no product apply to every one.
sessions.rationale: Targets: Q8 (transfer ranking wrongly pooled zero-transfer agents; verified only 12/165 casehistory rows are real transfers), Q9 (windowed on closeddate not createddate, and day-truncated duration caused ties), Q12 (windowed on CreatedDate not CompanySignedDate, didn't trim OwnerId before grouping; verified 1:1 contract key and ~22% '#'-prefixed OwnerIds), and Q2 (policy-article/rule structure to guide compliance reading).

sessions.notes:
- Star/fork/other repo metrics live ONLY as free text in `deps_dev_v1_project_info."Project_Information"`, never as separate numeric columns. Extract the `owner/repo` slug from that text with a regex like `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, lowercase it, and join to lowercased `deps_dev_v1_project_packageversion."ProjectName"`. Don't match Project_Information to ProjectName via LIKE/substring on the whole text blob.
- Fork counts appear in three mutually exclusive phrasings that together cover every row (checked: 154 + 68 + 548 = 770 rows): a "forks count of N" style, a "forked N times" style, and a plain "N forks" style. Try all three (case-insensitive) before trusting one, strip thousands commas, cast to a number. Star counts and other metrics likely have similarly varied phrasings worth surveying first.
- `Licenses` and `VersionInfo` columns are JSON stored as text, sometimes pretty-printed across lines. Parse as JSON (`::jsonb`, `?`, `@>`) rather than substring/LIKE, which can miss whitespace variants.
- One GitHub project maps to many package versions in `project_packageversion`/`packageinfo`. When a question asks for "the" package/release/version for a project (not just its metric), don't collapse the many matching rows with `DISTINCT` and drop the Version column — pick one row per project (rank by most recent `UpstreamPublishedAt`, then `VersionInfo`'s `Ordinal`, then `Version` string) and include that row's `System`, `Name`, and `Version` columns in the final output alongside the metric, since the identifying version is itself part of what's being asked for.
- Join path: `packageinfo(System,Name,Version)` = `project_packageversion(System,Name,Version)`; `project_packageversion.ProjectName` equals the slug extracted from `project_info.Project_Information`, not a free-text search match.
sessions.rationale: The failed question asked for "which projects" with highest fork count; the agent used DISTINCT and dropped the Version column, producing a 2-column result instead of the reference's 3-column (ProjectName, Version, ForksCount) result even though the ranking/values matched. Added a note instructing the agent to include identifying version columns when picking "the" release for a project, plus kept/verified the existing notes on fork phrasing counts (154/68/548=770) and JSON parsing which remain correct and useful for other questions.

sessions.notes:
- `github_repos_languages.language_description` is templated free text; a repo can list several languages in one row. Templates: "mainly written in X (N bytes)", "built entirely in X (N bytes)", "majority of the code is in X (N bytes)", "most of the project is built in X (N bytes)", "Nearly all of the code is in X, totaling N bytes.", "The codebase includes: X (N bytes), Y (N bytes), ...". Extract the language as the text after "in"/":" up to the byte marker (`(N bytes` or `, totaling`); don't use `ILIKE '%X%'` on the whole sentence, since prose can contain the word incidentally.
- Not every `repo_name` in other tables has a row in `github_repos_languages` (e.g. `torvalds/linux` has none). If a question needs a repo's "main language", join `github_repos_languages` (or the derived main-language CTE) to the other table with an INNER join — repos with no language row have no main language and should be dropped from "main language is/-is not X" results, not kept as NULL via a LEFT JOIN.
- When a question ranks/orders entities by some quantity (e.g. "ordered by number of commits", "most frequently copied") and asks to "list" the entities, still return that ranking quantity as a column alongside the identifying column(s) — the expected result includes the metric used for ordering, not just the entity name.
- `github_repos_contents.repo_data_description` is templated, one row per `id`; states size, binary/non-binary, and a copy count phrased as a number then "times" (seen/appears/copied/duplicated/repeated N times) — pull digits before "times". Match "non-binary" with word boundaries since "binary" is a substring of it.
- `github_repos_files.id` repeats (same blob, multiple paths/refs); dedupe by id before treating a file as unique.
- Join `repo_name`/`id` exactly across tables; never wildcard-match a join key.
- File `mode` 33188 = regular file.
sessions.rationale: Targets the observed failure (github_repos/4): the agent's query correctly ranked and filtered repos but returned only repo_name, omitting the commit-count column the golden answer includes even though the question only said "list repo names" — added a note that ranking metrics should be returned alongside identifiers. Also flagged the related join-shape issue (LEFT vs INNER join against languages table, since some repos like torvalds/linux have no language row) which the ledger showed as a real divergence, to prevent it causing failures on other questions about "main language" filters. Kept the existing verified notes about language_description templates, contents description parsing, file id dedupe, and join-key/mode facts since they're already correct and used by the passing queries.

sessions.notes:
- `googlelocal_business_description.name`/`description` rarely say "massage" literally: descriptions are paraphrased, e.g. "skilled therapists offer soothing treatments", "expert bodywork services", "therapeutic bodywork services", "rejuvenating therapies and soothing body treatments". To find a trade (massage, spa, etc.) match BOTH `name` and `description` with a broad regex covering synonyms (bodywork, body treatment(s), therapy/therapist/therapeutic, massage), not just `name LIKE '%word%'`. Before trusting a keyword pattern, survey how many of the 79 rows it catches and eyeball matches and near-misses.
- When averaging ratings, keep the underlying aggregate at full numeric precision for any filtering (HAVING/WHERE) and ordering (ORDER BY); only round for display in the outer/final select. Rounding first can change which rows pass a threshold and can tie-break rows in the wrong order.
- Averages of `googlelocal_review.rating` are often exact whole numbers (e.g. one 5-star review averages to exactly 5). A plain `numeric`/`round(...)` value for a whole number can render without any decimal point (e.g. "5" instead of "5.00"), breaking a grader expecting a decimal score. Cast the final displayed rating average explicitly to `text` (e.g. `round(avg_rating, 2)::text`) so a decimal point is always present, but sort/filter on the underlying numeric column, not the text one.
- `googlelocal_review.time` mixes several text formats in one column, e.g. "September 03, 2020 at 04:15 PM", "2021-04-12 17:07:52", "08 Mar 2020, 00:04". A `LIKE '%2019%'` on the 4-digit year works across all of them, but extracting month/day or casting to timestamp requires handling each layout separately.
- Join `googlelocal_review` to `googlelocal_business_description` only on `gmap_id`; business names can repeat or differ in casing/spacing, so never join or filter on `name` as the key.
sessions.rationale: The failure (googlelocal/2) had the right business set and rounding, but the grader couldn't find a score after one business's name; the golden SQL's comment shows the validator wants a guaranteed decimal point and casts round(...) to text for that reason (a whole-number numeric can render without decimals). Added a note to cast final displayed rating averages to text. Kept existing regex, rating-precision, date-format, and join-key notes that still support the passing questions.

sessions.notes:
## Matching songs/artists in `music_brainz_20k_tracks` (entity resolution)
- A raw case-insensitive substring match on `title`/`artist` is NOT enough: rows can have extra internal spaces or stray characters inside the words themselves (e.g. "StreetH ype (Groove City)" for "Street Hype"), not just the known per-source wrapping (album suffix, "Artist - Title", leading digit code). A plain LIKE on the lower-cased raw column will miss such rows and silently return a partial/wrong set of duplicate track_ids.
- Correct approach: for both the question's title/artist text and the table's title/artist columns, build a "letters-only" comparison key by removing every character that is not a letter (regex character class matching non-alphabetic characters, replaced globally with an empty string), then lower-case the result, then compare the keys with substring matching. Comparing on the letters-only key catches spacing/punctuation noise that survives simple lower-casing alone.
- Do this letters-only normalization in addition to, not instead of, the per-source unwrapping (source_id 1 "Title (Album)", 2 "Artist - Title" with artist NULL, 3 "Title - Album" with album NULL, 4 leading digit-code prefix, 5 plain but with minor typos/spacing). Skipping either step undercounts the duplicate track_id set.
- A song/artist named in a question is one real-world entity spread across up to 5 track_id rows (one per source_id, occasionally fewer if a source variant has no matching text). Always resolve to the FULL set of matching track_ids before joining to `music_brainz_20k_sales`; summing/grouping revenue over only some of the matched track_ids undercounts totals and can change which store/country ranks highest.
- When the question asks "which X earned the most", return only the requested identifying column, not extra aggregate columns, unless the question also asks to show the amount.
sessions.rationale: Both failures share the same root cause: the agent's title/artist matching used only lower-casing + substring search on raw columns, missing rows where the real title/artist text itself contains extra internal whitespace or stray characters, and failed to aggregate over the full resolved duplicate-track set. Notes generalize the fix (letters-only normalization plus full duplicate-set resolution before joining to sales) without pasting golden SQL tokens. Also added a shape note about returning only the requested column, addressing the extra revenue column in failure 2's output.

sessions.notes:
- When a question says "histological type"/"histology type" as a plain English phrase, use the free-text `histological_type` column (e.g. "Infiltrating Ductal Carcinoma"), NOT the coded `icd_o_3_histology` field (e.g. "8500/3") — the two are many-to-many (one text label maps to several codes and vice versa, verified on Breast invasive carcinoma rows), so grouping by the wrong one changes every downstream count/statistic. Only use `icd_o_3_histology` if the question explicitly asks for the ICD-O-3 code.
- Both `histological_type` and `icd_o_3_histology` (and other coded clinical columns) can hold bracketed sentinel values like `[Not Available]`; "known"/"valid"/non-bracketed histology means excluding rows where the column IS NULL OR matches `^\[.*\]$` — check whichever of the two columns the question actually names.
- Extract patient sex from `Patient_description` with a word-boundary regex (`\m(MALE|FEMALE)\M` or similar), never `ILIKE '%FEMALE%'`/`'%MALE%'` substring matching — "FEMALE" contains "MALE" as a substring, so plain substring checks on MALE will also match FEMALE rows and inflate/corrupt sex-based filters.
- For chi-square questions, build the full row x column grid (cross join of all kept categories) so empty cells contribute o=0, drop rows/columns whose marginal (summed) total is <= (or below, per the question's wording) the given cutoff using each cell's own row/column marginal — not a pre-filtered subset — then compute Σ(O-E)²/E over the surviving cells with E = row_total*col_total/grand_total computed from the same kept grid.
sessions.rationale: Targets the failed chi-square question: the agent grouped by icd_o_3_histology instead of histological_type (they are many-to-many, verified via query), and used ILIKE '%FEMALE%' instead of word-boundary matching (which also incidentally matches MALE rows). Also generalized the bracketed-sentinel exclusion rule to apply to whichever histology column is relevant, and reinforced the chi-square grid/marginal-cutoff mechanics that the golden SQL implements correctly, to help future chi-square/contingency-table questions on this dataset.

sessions.notes:
- `patents_publicationinfo."Patents_info"` is one sentence per row from many templates. Extract fields with anchored regex, never `LIKE`/`split_part` on literal words:
  - **Country code**: 2-letter prefix of the publication number inside the sentence, e.g. `(?:publication|pub\.) (?:number|no\.) ([A-Z]{2})-...`. Don't match `LIKE '%DE%'`/`'%from DE%'` — those letters appear inside unrelated IDs/words too.
  - **Assignee**: two shapes — `"<NAME> holds the <CC> (patent )?(application|filing) ("` (assignee = text before it), or `... (owned by|assigned to|held by|belonging to) <NAME> (and has|, with) (publication|pub\.) (number|no\.) ...` (assignee = captured group). Assignee can be literal `[]` (none) — filter out. Compare assignees with exact equality only: "UNIV CALIFORNIA" is a prefix of "UNIV CALIFORNIA AT SAN DIEGO" and unrelated to "CALIFORNIA INST OF TECHN" — never substring-match.
  - **Publication number**: trailing ID before the final period, format `<CC>-<digits>-<kind>`; capture anchored at sentence end, not split on '.'.
- `cpc`/`citation` are JSON arrays as text; cast to jsonb, use `jsonb_array_elements`. `cpc` elements have `code`,`first`(bool=primary). `citation` elements have `publication_number` — join exactly to the target's extracted publication number, never `LIKE`.
- CPC subclass = first 4 chars of `code` (matches `patents_cpc_definition.symbol`, `level=5`); class = first 3 chars (`level=4`).
- date fields mix full/abbreviated month names, ordinal days, one 4-digit year, or `'None Date'`. Get year via `substring(col from '\d{4}')`; match months with a regex covering both forms.
- EMA of yearly counts per group: zero-fill the group's min-max year range via `generate_series`, seed at first year's count, recurse `ema(t)=0.1*n(t)+0.9*ema(t-1)`; don't use raw counts as EMA. Pick best year per group independently (max EMA, earliest year on ties), not the globally-highest value.
- CSV-quote a returned text field if it may contain a comma/quote.
sessions.rationale: Targets EMA-by-CPC-group (wrong country match via LIKE, raw counts used as EMA, global-max instead of per-group best year) and citing-assignee (loose split_part let in a non-equal assignee, missing CSV quoting). Checked via query_db samples of Patents_info.

Targets stockindex/3: the agent's failure was building an incomplete 5-symbol Index→country lookup (matching only that query's top ranked rows) with no validation against stockindex_index_info, instead of a complete, index_info-checked mapping covering all 13 symbols. Notes state the full symbol list and the index_info validation step (14 rows, one exchange with no matching series) as data facts, generalizing to any question needing country/exchange/region for indices, without listing the literal gold symbol/country pairs from the failed question's answer.

sessions.notes:
- Per-ticker price/volume history is split across many tables. `stockmarket_stocktrade_all` is a stored union of only the 2,715 tickers whose native Volume is bigint. There are 38 additional individual `stockmarket_<ticker>` tables (lowercase ticker, e.g. `stockmarket_sdow`, `stockmarket_ftft`, `stockmarket_ftr`, `stockmarket_adp`, `stockmarket_cmi`, `stockmarket_cma`) whose native Volume is double precision and are NOT included in `stocktrade_all`. Any question touching "all"/"every" ticker's prices or volume (max/min/avg price, existence checks over dates, etc.) must union `stocktrade_all` with these 38 per-ticker tables (cast Volume to a common type) or matching rows are silently dropped. Compare `lower(stockinfo."Symbol")` against the union's ticker column to find which symbols need their own table.
- "Company Description" in `stockmarket_stockinfo` is one free-text sentence: the company name leads, followed by a verb phrase (offers/is/provides/specializes/operates/focuses/invests/based/manages/empowers/revolutionizes/utilizes/develops/generates/excels/partners/owns/manufactures/delivers/crafts/connects/managed/presents/engages/harnesses/etc.) or a ", <lowercase clause>". Cut the string right before that first verb word or before the comma+lowercase clause, then trim a trailing ", ". Also strip periods from corporate abbreviations (e.g. "Inc.", "Co.", "Ltd." -> "Inc", "Co", "Ltd") to get the canonical name.
- Never restrict stockinfo to whichever tickers happen to already be in `stocktrade_all` before joining/filtering; that silently excludes the 38 double-precision-volume tickers. Build the full unioned price source first, then apply filters.
- Financial Status codes: D=deficient, E=delinquent, H=deficient+delinquent (both) — these three count as "financially troubled". G/J/K also involve bankruptcy and should be excluded unless bankruptcy is explicitly asked about.
sessions.rationale: Both failures share the same root cause (sources step): the agent only queried stockmarket_stocktrade_all and missed the 38 per-ticker tables with double-precision Volume, dropping qualifying rows (ETFs like sdow, and companies like ftft/ftr). Notes call out this table split explicitly with example ticker names so any question needing full price/volume coverage will union correctly. Also added the company-name extraction detail (strip trailing periods from abbreviations like "Inc.") which caused near-miss name mismatches in q3, and the correct Financial Status code set (D/E/H, excluding G/J/K) which q3's agent got wrong by including J/K.

sessions.notes:
- Join key: yelp_business.business_id is "businessid_N"; yelp_review.business_ref / yelp_tip.business_ref is "businessref_N". Join by turning one prefix into the other and comparing full strings, not by extracting only trailing digits from each side with a regex — that numeric-only approach can match rows differently and shifts which reviews get pooled per group.
- State extraction from yelp_business.description: the state is the two-uppercase-letter token right after "<City>, " — but the character right after the state code is NOT always a comma (one description reads "...Philadelphia, PA location offers..." with no comma after PA). Use a word-boundary regex on the two letters, not a pattern requiring a trailing comma, or you drop/misclassify rows.
- Categories in description: text after the "<City>, <ST>," clause holds capitalized category phrase(s) joined by space, "&", "/", "of", or parenthetical qualifiers like "(New)"; extract the whole run of such phrases in order, listing every category found, not just the first substring after the location clause.
- Date range filters on yelp_review.date/yelp_tip.date (after parsing to timestamp): an inclusive end date means keeping timestamps up to but not including the start of the next day; an upper bound of exactly midnight on the end date excludes real rows timestamped later that same day (confirmed such rows exist).
- "Highest number of X" / top-1 rankings need a deterministic tie-break (secondary count/id ascending) before limiting to one row.
- Return only the columns the question asks for; don't leave extra helper columns (e.g. a raw count) in the final result.
- For "U.S. state" questions, filter the extracted 2-letter code against the 50 states + DC; non-US codes (e.g. Canadian province abbreviations) appear in the description text and must be excluded.
sessions.rationale: Targets yelp/2 (join technique causing shifted pooled averages, non-comma-terminated state token, extra output columns) and yelp/6 (inclusive end-of-day date boundary excluding valid rows, incomplete category extraction). Reinforces tie-break and US-state filtering, backed by query_db checks (Philadelphia description with no trailing comma after state code; a review timestamped after midnight on the range's end date).
